::: {.statx-chapter-banner}
## Expand the statistical toolkit

This lab will use resampling, robust methods, and careful data workflows to address realistic analytical complications.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

1. Use a nonparametric method when its assumptions and target are appropriate.
2. Estimate uncertainty with the bootstrap.
3. Compare predictive models with cross-validation.
4. Diagnose missingness and outline principled next steps.

## Planned workflow

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 1. Robust comparison

Contrast a classical and nonparametric analysis on the same data.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 2. Bootstrap uncertainty

Resample observations to build an empirical distribution for an estimate.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 3. Cross-validation

Evaluate competing models across repeated training and validation splits.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 4. Real-data complications

Map missing values, discuss plausible mechanisms, and avoid automatic deletion.
:::
:::

## Deliverables

- A classical-versus-robust comparison
- A bootstrap interval and visualization
- A cross-validation summary
- A missing-data decision note
